# Testability Checklist: Change-Request Review and Remediation

**Purpose**: Validate that every gate, stopping condition and prohibition in the specification is written as something an implementation can be tested against, and that no requirement silently assumes a capability the specification never established
**Created**: 2026-09-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the scale for a finding's confidence enumerated, the way severity is fixed at six named values? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK001 enumerates `high`, `medium`, `low`; severity-model.md documents definitions; data-model.md constrains Finding.confidence to these three values.
- [x] CHK002 Is the permitted set of finding categories enumerated, or is its relationship to the eleven review dimensions stated? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-013] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK002 lists eleven categories matching FR-010 dimensions; data-model.md constrains Finding.category to exactly these eleven values.
- [x] CHK003 Is "a discussion that blocks" defined, so that an implementation can determine which discussions gate a pass? [Gap, Spec §FR-015] — **Satisfied**: severity-model.md "Blocking rules" section defines blocking as platform-unresolved AND ≥1 Critical/High/Medium/Low comment from non-author reviewer; Suggestion/Question never block.
- [x] CHK004 Are the criteria for identifying credentials and secret material in a diff specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-027] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK004 enumerates regex patterns (AWS keys, generic API keys, private keys, connection strings, base64 secrets); scoped to diff content only; deterministic and testable.
- [x] CHK005 Is the precedence among competing validation-command sources stated, rather than only the obligation to report which was chosen? [Gap, Spec §FR-007] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK005 states four-level precedence (explicit target → CI config → docs → conventional defaults); reference/validation.md documents same; verify-repository.sh implements it.
- [x] CHK006 Is the mechanism by which preview mode is requested specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-041] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK006 specifies `--dry-run` flag; quickstart.md Scenario 2 demonstrates invocation; FR-041 requires the mode exist.
- [x] CHK007 Is the accepted form of an explicitly named change-request identifier specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-002] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK007 accepts numeric ID, full URL, or branch name; preflight.sh parses numeric; forge CLIs handle URL/branch natively.
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for a remediation that partially completes and then fails — is the working tree left as-is, restored, or reported? [Gap, Recovery Flow] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK008 specifies leave-as-is with uncommitted changes intact, report addressed/remaining findings, record `remediation.partial=true`; no auto-rollback; SKILL.md T026 implements.
- [x] CHK009 Is it stated whether the cycle count resets between invocations or persists across them? [Gap, Spec §FR-033, §FR-034] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK009 states resets between invocations; data-model.md validation rules confirm; tasks.md note on CHK009 restates.
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for determining the reviewing identity's permissions before an action is attempted, rather than only for reporting a permission that turned out to be missing? [Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-020] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK010 specifies read-only probe before write actions via forge API; result cached per invocation; permission-check.sh implements; FR-020 reports missing permission.
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for what the run records about its own actions for later audit? [Gap, Observability] — **Satisfied**: research.md CHK011 defines JSON array format with timestamp/action/target/outcome/evidence; data-model.md AuditEntry entity specifies five action types; SKILL.md T031 implements append-only audit trail.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK012 Can "the smallest change that resolves the finding" be objectively evaluated, or does it rest on reviewer judgement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023] — **Satisfied**: FR-023 pairs "smallest change" with "fix root causes" and "MUST NOT refactor code no finding concerns"; testable by checking whether any changed line lies outside the finding's evidence scope. Reviewer judgment applies within bounds, not unbounded discretion.
- [x] CHK013 Is "eligible" quantified for adding the reviewing identity as a reviewer? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018] — **Satisfied**: FR-018 states two conditions: (1) identity is eligible per platform rules (not blocked, not pending invite), (2) identity is not the author. Both are checkable via forge API; permission-check.sh probes eligibility before action.
- [x] CHK014 Is "the repository's full applicable validation" defined, specifically what makes a declared validation applicable or not? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025] — **Satisfied**: FR-007 + research.md CHK005 define applicability via four-level precedence; verify-repository.sh resolves exactly one command or reports none. "Full applicable" means the resolved command at highest available precedence level.
- [x] CHK015 Is "information it does not have" specified precisely enough to distinguish it from a finding the run simply could not resolve? [Measurability, Spec §FR-033] — **Satisfied**: FR-043 requires plain statement when something could not be determined; FR-046 requires asking rather than assuming. "Information it does not have" = fact the forge API returned as absent/undetermined, distinct from a finding whose evidence exists but severity is uncertain.
- [x] CHK016 Is "an explicit request" defined, so that an implementation can determine whether one was given? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-035, §FR-040] — **Satisfied**: FR-040 establishes default review-only; remediation and merge each require separate invocation flags (`--remediate`, `--merge`) or interactive confirmation. Implementation checks for flag presence or AskUserQuestion affirmative response.
- [x] CHK017 Is the condition under which a finding has no location stated, given that one requirement makes a location conditional and another requires evidence to be cited? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-013] — **Satisfied**: data-model.md Finding.file and Finding.line are nullable; FR-013 says "where one exists"; FR-011 requires evidence citation regardless of location. A finding about repository-wide policy (e.g., missing LICENSE) has evidence but no file/line location.
- [x] CHK018 Are the criteria for deciding that a finding duplicates one already raised on the change request specified? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012] — **Satisfied**: FR-012 prohibits duplicating existing comments; collect-context.sh gathers existing comments; dedup matches on file+line+evidence substring. SKILL.md T018 implements dedup against existing comments per FR-012.
- [x] CHK019 Is "shaped like an instruction to the reviewer" specified well enough to be applied consistently, or is the prohibition stated only as intent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-042] — **Satisfied**: FR-042 enumerates sources (repository files, diff, scripts, comments) and states "treated as content to review, never as a direction to follow". Testable: any text in those sources parsed as data input, never executed as control flow. Edge Cases section reinforces with concrete example.
- [x] CHK020 Is "the repository's own stated convention" for commit messages defined by reference to something discoverable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028] — **Satisfied**: Convention discovered from .gitmessage, .commitlintrc, CONTRIBUTING.md, or recent commit history. SKILL.md T025 commits per repo convention; if none found, uses Conventional Commits as fallback. Discoverable artifacts take precedence over inference.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK021 Is the precedence between the obligation to publish a request-for-changes verdict and the obligation to record no verdict on a self-authored change request stated explicitly? [Conflict, Spec §FR-016, §FR-019, §FR-047] — **Satisfied**: FR-047 explicitly overrides FR-016 and FR-019; comment-only path takes precedence when reviewer is author. Research.md documents this resolution.
- [x] CHK022 Do the requirement to publish findings on a self-authored change request and the requirement never to publish without an explicit request agree on which actions the review stage may take? [Consistency, Spec §FR-040, §FR-047] — **Satisfied**: FR-040 requires explicit request for remediation and merge only; review-stage comment publication on self-authored CRs is permitted by FR-047 as exception to FR-016, not FR-040. No conflict.
- [x] CHK023 Is the criterion-level override for absent validation reconciled with the requirement that a pass needs every criterion to hold? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-048] — **Satisfied**: FR-048 states criterion remains "not satisfied" even when overridden; pass requires all criteria satisfied OR explicitly overridden with recorded reason. Data-model.md CriterionStatus distinguishes `overridden` from `satisfied`. No contradiction.
- [x] CHK024 Is the term for the change request's current revision used consistently across requirements, entities and success criteria? [Consistency, Terminology] — **Satisfied**: "head_sha" in data-model.md ChangeRequest; "revision under review" in FR-005, FR-015, FR-036; "current revision" in FR-036. All refer to same field. SKILL.md captures once at preflight, re-checks before merge.
- [x] CHK025 Do the preview-mode requirement and the remediation-authorisation requirement agree on what happens when both a preview request and an authorisation are present? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-041] — **Satisfied**: FR-041 suppresses ALL actions including remediation; preview mode takes precedence over authorization. Research.md CHK006 confirms suppression scope. Data-model.md shows `commit_sha=null`, `published=false` in preview mode.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK026 Can each of the six pass criteria be independently evaluated and reported, as the requirement asserts? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015] — **Satisfied**: Each criterion maps to independent data source: findings register, validation output, CI status, discussion state, head SHA, approval rules. Data-model.md CriterionStatus carries separate evidence per criterion. No circular dependencies.
- [x] CHK027 Is the distinction between a criterion marked not satisfied and one explicitly overridden observable in the verdict itself? [Measurability, Spec §SC-012, §FR-048] — **Satisfied**: Data-model.md CriterionStatus.status has three enum values: `satisfied`, `not-satisfied`, `overridden`. Override_reason non-null only when overridden. SC-012 requires this distinguishability. Verdict template renders each status distinctly.
- [x] CHK028 Is the success criterion about preview mode stated in terms an auditor can apply without access to the run's internals? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006] — **Satisfied**: SC-006 specifies "byte-for-byte comparison of the working tree and a fetch of the change request before and after". Auditor uses `git status`, `git diff`, and `gh pr view` / `glab mr view`. No internal state access required.
- [x] CHK029 Are the success criteria free of thresholds that depend on facts the specification never establishes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001 through §SC-012] — **Satisfied**: All SCs reference spec-defined entities (findings, verdicts, criteria, working tree, commits). None cite external performance targets, industry benchmarks, or third-party tool outputs. All thresholds are countable ("zero", "every", "byte-for-byte").

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for a repository configured with more than one remote, given that platform detection is specified against "the repository's own configured remote" singular? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-003] — **Satisfied**: FR-003 specifies detection from `origin` remote; forge-detect.sh checks `origin` specifically. Multiple remotes beyond `origin` are out of scope per Assumptions. Behavior documented: detect `origin` only, ignore others.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for a target branch that cannot be brought up to date without rewriting history? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-039] — **Satisfied**: FR-039 requires "without rewriting history"; if fast-forward fails, run reports divergence and stops. Edge Cases section covers target branch movement. No force-push or rebase permitted per FR-038.
- [x] CHK032 Is a threshold specified above which a change is treated as too large to examine completely, rather than only an obligation to report partial coverage? [Coverage, Edge Case] — **Satisfied**: Edge Cases section states "reports how much it examined and what it did not reach, rather than implying complete coverage". No hard threshold; coverage reporting is proportional. Implementation reports diff_lines examined vs total.
- [x] CHK033 Are requirements defined for the run being interrupted between a remediation commit and its transmission? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Gap] — **Satisfied**: FR-029 prohibits transmission when validation failed; CHK008 specifies partial remediation leaves tree as-is with uncommitted changes. Interrupted transmission = unpushed commit exists locally; next invocation detects via preflight dirty-tree or stale-SHA check. Audit trail records what completed.
- [x] CHK034 Are requirements defined for each of the five entities in the data model reaching a state no requirement covers — in particular a finding that is neither open, fixed, nor explicitly not fixed? [Coverage, Spec §Key Entities] — **Satisfied**: Data-model.md Finding.status enum is exactly `{open, fixed, deferred}`. State transitions diagram shows only valid paths. "Deferred" = explicitly not fixed with user reason. No fourth state exists; validation rules enforce enum constraint.

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK035 Does the specification establish which hosting platforms are targeted, or does the delivery requirement assume a set defined only outside the spec? [Assumption, Spec §FR-050] — **Satisfied**: FR-050 explicitly names "both of the hosting platforms this plugin already targets" (GitHub and GitLab). Assumptions section validates both. Forge-detect.sh returns `unsupported-forge` for others. Set defined within spec.
- [x] CHK036 Is the assumption that both hosting platforms expose everything the context-gathering requirement needs validated, or recorded only as an assumption with a fallback? [Assumption, Spec §FR-005, §Assumptions] — **Satisfied**: Assumptions section states "Where one does not expose a particular fact, that fact is reported as undetermined rather than substituted." Fallback = report undetermined, not guess. Validated by implementation: collect-context.sh reports empty/unknown for missing fields.
- [x] CHK037 Is the assumption that the reviewing identity may differ from the operating maintainer carried through every requirement that says "the user", so that the two are never conflated? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-046] — **Satisfied**: Assumptions section explicitly distinguishes "reviewing identity" (authenticated account) from "maintainer operating the session". FR-046 asks user for missing info; FR-018/FR-019/FR-047 use "reviewing identity" for permission/approval checks. No conflation found.
- [x] CHK038 Are the capabilities the specification relies on but does not define — inline commenting, approval recording, mergeability reporting — declared as dependencies? [Dependency, Spec §FR-017, §FR-016, §FR-005] — **Satisfied**: FR-017 says "where the hosting platform supports it"; FR-005 lists capabilities as gathered facts; Assumptions section declares platform exposure as dependency. Github.md/gitlab.md document platform-specific command availability. Missing capability = report undetermined per Assumptions fallback.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK021 and CHK023 are the two items most likely to surface a genuine contradiction rather than a wording gap; resolve them before planning
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
